title: Consolidate tenant KMS entitlement with temporal RBAC leases and audit lineage
author: Anya Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated jurisdictions need a single, auditable flow that ties tenant-scoped KMS usage to short-lived operator RBAC leases and produces cryptographically verifiable audit lineage. This change consolidates three related patterns: (1) tenant KMS entitlement checks, (2) temporal RBAC leases for operator/service accounts, and (3) audit-lineage signatures that persist provenance across async fanouts. The goal is to prevent long-lived operator key access, make KMS selection deterministic by residency policy, and ensure every KMS call can be traced to a lease token in the audit log.

What this PR does: introduces a new temporal-lease service that mints short-lived operator leases bound to tenant, region, and allowed KMS provider; augments the policy-enforcer to evaluate lease-scoped RBAC v2 assertions; extends kms-allocator to refuse key unwraps unless a valid lease token is present; and updates audit-proxy to attach lineage signatures (sha256 over request metadata + lease id) to all forwarded entries. Also adds integration tests and migration scripts that add new indexes to the audit store for lease_id and lineage_signature.

Compatibility notes: the flow is backward-compatible for existing service-to-service calls because the policy-enforcer accepts either existing operator tokens or a temporal lease. However, newly deployed Private installations can opt-in to strict enforcement (feature flag: enforce_temporal_leases). A runtime-config flag controls whether kms-allocator enforces region pinning by default.

Implementation summary (single string): created temporal-lease microservice (Go) with endpoints POST /leases (create), GET /leases/{id} (introspect), DELETE /leases/{id}; added LeaseIssuer and LeaseVerifier libraries used by policy-enforcer and kms-allocator; added database migrations to audits.events to index lease_id and lineage_signature; updated kms-allocator to require X-Lease-Token header on unwrap calls when enforcement enabled; extended audit-proxy to compute lineage_signature and store it as audit.header.lineage_signature; updated RBAC v2 evaluation to include lease-bound attributes (lease.exp, lease.region, lease.allowed_kms); added TypeScript SDK changes (redwood-sdk-typescript) to surface createLease helper; included CLI tooling for grant/renew/evict leases in redwood-ctl; added end-to-end test suite that runs policy-enforcer+kms-allocator+audit-proxy to assert lineage at rest.

review_comments:
Lena Brooks (reviewer): 'High-level: makes sense, but we need to ensure the lineage_signature format is stable and documented for long-term retention. Please add a vector for signature algorithm rotation.'
Anya (author): 'Added a section to docs/security/temporal-leases.md describing algorithm identifier (sha256+ed25519), rotation plan, and how to backfill signatures if rotation happens; also added a signature_version field in the audit header.'
Harish Rao (reviewer): 'Concern: the index on lineage_signature will balloon. Can we instead store a hash prefix and index that? Also confirm retention policy stores full signature for legal/audit needs.'
Anya: 'Updated migration to add lineage_signature_prefix (first 8 bytes hex) and indexed that instead of full signature; full signature retained in storage but not indexed. Note added tests to ensure prefix collision extremely unlikely in our workload.'
Marta Vasile (reviewer): 'Operational question: what happens if a temporal lease service is not available? How do we fail gracefully for Dedicated customers?'
Anya: 'Policy-enforcer falls back to operator token behavior when enforce_temporal_leases=false; the helm chart adds a health-check and sidecar caching path, and we included a 72-hour grace mode for Dedicated upgrade bakeouts. Documented in ops guide.'
Follow-ups: small nit fixes to log messages and added additional unit tests. All addressed in subsequent commits.

release_notes: Added temporal operator leases for tenant-scoped KMS usage, RBAC v2 lease-bound assertions, and audit lineage signatures to improve proof-of-use and data residency enforcement. Feature is behind a runtime flag and off by default for Private installs. See docs/security/temporal-leases.md for migration and rollout guidance.
